focus: A9 version-aware hooks and guards: per-rule v1/v2 validity of the five opencode-run hard rules, the dispatch classifier's opencode2 blind spot, the Pi preflight guard, and whether .opencode/hooks is host-loaded
answeredQuestions: How must hooks, guards and plugin dependencies become version-aware so neither version breaks?

graphEvents.label: command-flag-for-slash-prompt hard-blocks v2 where --command does not exist
opencode2 is invisible to every dispatch guard and lint
per-plugin directory layout breaks every ../hooks import depth

label: v2 run flags confirmed from the captured help: --model is provider/model#variant; --agent, --format default|json, --file, --title, --thinking, --continue, --session, --fork, --auto, --server, --standalone exist; --command, --share, --variant, --port, --attach, --dir and --pure do not. --print-logs is a global flag whose server logs require --standalone, and --log-level takes lowercase enumerated choices, so the v1 remediation recipe inside explicit-model-required does not work verbatim on v2.

Per-rule v1/v2 validity: stdin-redirect-required is valid on both (wider hang window on v2, which attaches to a background service before reading the message); explicit-model-required stays behaviorally correct on both because its check is format-agnostic, but its remediation text is stale on v2; no-bare-agent-general remains advisory and unverified on v2; command-flag-for-slash-prompt is INVALID on v2 because v2 run has no --command yet the rule is severity error, which evaluate maps to block, so a correct v2 slash-command workflow is refused with no way to satisfy the guard; share-requires-confirmation is vacuous on v2 where --share does not exist.

opencode2 is invisible to every guard in four independent places: EXECUTOR_BASENAMES is an exact-name Set holding only 'opencode'; directExecutor returns null for a non-member before reading the subcommand; the opencode-run arm and the dispatch-evidence regex both use \bopencode\s+run\b, whose word boundary fails against 'opencode2 run'; and the stdin rule's shape list plus its pipe carve-out repeat the same literal. The result is kind 'none' at inspectDispatch, so the Pi guard returns early and the hard rules are never evaluated. The failure is fail-open, not fail-closed.

Name-based version inference is refuted in both directions: after the official installer 'opencode' IS v2, so the v1 rule set is applied to a v2 CLI and command-flag-for-slash-prompt hard-blocks it; and the local side-by-side user has opencode=1.19.3 with opencode2=v2.0.32, which no guard recognises at all. Mis-lint for the installed-default user, silent hole for the side-by-side user.
No rule may demand a flag that does not exist on the target version: a severity-error rule must be satisfiable by every version it is applied to, or it must be scoped out by appliesTo.

Proposed version-aware matcher design: (1) name-admit only in the matcher, widening EXECUTOR_BASENAMES to opencode2 and every \bopencode\s+run\b literal to opencode\d*, which can only add coverage and cannot break a v1 user; (2) add appliesTo [v1|v2|both] plus optional v2Replacement to each rule object, defaulting to both when absent so today's sidecars keep working; (3) resolve the version tri-state (v1|v2|unknown) from one memoised --version probe with a timeout, parsing both observed formats by stripping an optional 'opencode v' prefix; (4) degrade 'unknown' to the rule intersection so the environment is conservative-but-usable rather than blocked; (5) use command-shape evidence (--command/--share/--variant/--attach/--port/--dir/--pure for v1, --standalone and a #variant model value for v2) to override unknown and to widen to v1+v2 on mixed commands; (6) add the missing binaryOnPathCheck for opencode against the resolved binary.

.opencode/hooks is not a host-loaded concept on either version: it is a symlink to ../.skilled/hooks consumed only by ES-module imports from the repo's own plugins (e.g. '../hooks/dispatch/lib/dispatch-audit.mjs'), and its tree is a cross-runtime adapter layout (goal/ ships opencode, pi, cursor, devin and deliberately no claude). The only host-native hooks surface referenced anywhere in the repo is a user-level ~/.opencode/hooks.json behind [features].opencode_hooks, a different path and scope. No version work is needed inside the directory for host loading.

v2's per-plugin directory layout silently breaks the hook reachability of every plugin: all 16 plugins import at depth one ('../hooks/...'), which resolves to .opencode/hooks only while the plugin file sits flat at .opencode/plugins/<name>.js. Under .opencode/plugins/<name>/index.js the same import resolves to a nonexistent .opencode/plugins/hooks and the plugin fails at load time on v2 only. Cheapest fix if per-plugin directories are mandatory is a .opencode/plugins/hooks symlink rather than rebasing 16 import lines.

direction: Infer the OpenCode version from the binary name (opencode = v1, opencode2 = v2)
reason: Refuted in both directions: the official installer makes 'opencode' v2, and the local side-by-side pair is opencode=1.19.3 with opencode2=2.0.32. Name and version are uncorrelated, so the guards must resolve by --version.

direction: Treat .opencode/hooks as an OpenCode hook directory that needs version-gating
reason: Nothing on either host loads it. It is a symlink to ../.skilled/hooks reached only through relative module imports from the repo's plugins, with a cross-runtime adapter tree inside; the only host-native hooks surface found is the user-level ~/.opencode/hooks.json feature flag.
